sections.content: How many people are "pensions and insurance clerks and assistants"?

55,885 people

were counted on the census as "pensions and insurance clerks and assistants" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Pensions and insurance clerks and assistants provide general clerical support to senior colleagues and perform specialist clerical tasks in relation to the administration of pensions and insurance policies.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "pensions and insurance clerks and assistants", 17.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "pensions and insurance clerks and assistants" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "pensions and insurance clerks and assistants" included:

  • communication operators
  • nannies and au pairs
  • human resources administrative occupations

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "pensions and insurance clerks and assistants" there were more women than men (63% compared with 37%).

This means "pensions and insurance clerks and assistants" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "administrative occupations".

Men made up 37% and women made up 63% of "pensions and insurance clerks and assistants"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "pensions and insurance clerks and assistants" included:

  • bar and catering supervisors
  • charitable organisation managers and directors
  • project support officers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "pensions and insurance clerks and assistants" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "pensions and insurance clerks and assistants" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "pensions and insurance clerks and assistants", 10.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (78.4% compared with 21.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (97.5%) than self-employed (2.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
